title: Frontend: Event Emitter
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Event Emitter. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(commands). Commands on{id,event,once?}, off{id}, emit{event,value}. Each subscribed listener logs [id,value]. Emission uses subscription order and a snapshot; once subscriptions are removed before invocation. Return the log. IDs are unique per live subscription.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Store listeners per event and return an idempotent unsubscribe function.
alternativeApproaches: Add an async emit mode with a deliberate sequential versus parallel error policy.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Unsubscribe twice; add/remove during emit; reentrant emit.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
